findings.title: Latched failure during disposal can coexist with successful done
findings.observed: Actual unchanged helper done fulfilled with {code:0,signal:null} although fail had latched an error during awaited HOME disposal; subsequent finish rejected the same latched failure. Also reproduced through actual public-restart readiness timer at 45000ms, not only direct fail().
findings.mechanism: combine checks failure after action, before await lifecycle.stop()/dispose(); it does not re-read failure before its success return. Promise.race has already chosen the close branch. Readiness timer is only cleared after owned.done settles, so it can fire while removal is pending.
findings.repro: python3 run-contract-red.py: I1-F1 and I1-F1-public fail their required accepted=false assertion; control cases succeed. probes/critic.test.ts independently characterizes accepted=true and confirms later finish rejection.
findings.fix: Reconcile the latched primary failure after asynchronous cleanup and before publishing terminal success; aggregate it with distinct cleanup errors. Ensure readiness timer and terminal outcome ownership cannot disagree. Add slow-disposal/late-failure regression control.
findings.limits: Fake ChildProcess without PID/descendants, mocked fs.rm delayed for a finite interval, real helper and real readiness function. This proves an inconsistent helper terminal result, not a full PG fixture green: current consumers unconditionally call stop(), which will surface the latched failure. No observed PG/data/production impact.

findings.title: Store consumer DB cleanup still replaces original failure
findings.observed: After confirmed child join, rejection of cleanup(pool,executionId) replaces a pending assertion exception and skips pool.end(); pool.end rejection can likewise replace a pending primary error. Returned error has neither cause nor aggregate containing the primary.
findings.mechanism: primary is supplied only to stopCompleteChildren, which returns normally when children join; the following database cleanup and pool.end are bare awaits in the finally block.
findings.repro: Static actual consumer source and consumer-diff.patch establish the exact ordering. probes/critic.test.ts contains an authored, synthetic model of that finally ordering with stub cleanup; its paired success control preserves original assertion, its cleanup-error case returns only synthetic DB cleanup. run-contract-red.py fails the AggregateError contract assertion.
findings.fix: After a successful join, collect distinct DB cleanup and pool close errors while retaining primary as cause/member; attempt safe pool closure even if row cleanup fails. Keep DB cleanup forbidden when child join is unconfirmed.
findings.limits: The bare DB cleanup tail pre-existed this change; the modified finally still does not meet the newly frozen TH06 requirement. The probe is a control-flow model, not execution/import of either PG fixture or any application package body; no database was accessed.
